The Signal: A Higher Bid, Signed but Not Settled

The rumor has become a term sheet, and the price went up on the way. On July 17 Databricks announced a signed term sheet for a strategic funding round at a $188 billion post-money valuation, led by existing investor Coatue with participation from new and existing backers (company announcement, July 17, 2026). The company has not disclosed the size; press reports place it near $3 billion (press reports, July 17, 2026). The money is explicitly not in hand: the company expects the round to close later this summer, and the deal record carries it as announced and in progress, the thirteenth equity round (PitchBook financing note, August 7, 2026).

This is the July coverage's open question, resolved upward. The initiation note carried the reported $165 to 175 billion talks under the standing rule that unclosed financings are analyzed, never adopted, and the tracker held that line while the talks firmed. The signed term sheet lands $13 billion above the top of the talked range and 40% above the $134 billion completed mark set five months earlier (derived from the two marks). The size tells the same story the February round told: roughly $3 billion against February's $7.0 billion raise is a company building dry powder on its own schedule, raising because it wants to, not because it must (PitchBook deal record, February 9, 2026).

Figure 1. Post-money valuation marks, December 2024 to July 2026. Completed marks solid (company disclosures; PitchBook deal records); the July 17, 2026 term sheet hatched: signed at $188B, unclosed, not adopted in the base case until funds settle.

What happened is a price signal; what it means is a re-rate of the same engine. Nothing in the operating record moved with the announcement: the last dated print remains $6.9 billion of run-rate growing +80% YoY (company disclosure, June 16, 2026), gross margin remains 74% and guided lower, and the next scheduled disclosure is the September to October window. The bid moved, the business did not. At the completed mark the run-rate multiple is 19.4x; at the announced mark it is 27.2x on the identical June print (derived). The September print therefore decides which of those numbers the buyer actually paid.

Figure 2. Annualized revenue run-rate (bars, left axis) and year-over-year growth (line, right axis), company disclosures September 2025 to June 2026. No new print since June 16; the announced bid re-prices this same ladder.

The implication cuts two ways. For the base case, discipline holds: the $134 billion completed mark anchors valuation work until funds settle, and every figure in this note that depends on the mark is stated at both levels where the difference matters. For the forward view, the signal tier upgraded: a speculative range sourced to press became a company-confirmed price with a named lead. The watch item is no longer whether a round happens; it is whether the close lands on schedule, and what the first post-money print shows.
